mycinema.manual.chapter.start.title: MyCinema Manual
mycinema.manual.chapter.start.body:
Read in order for a first setup, or use the chapter buttons. The guide follows your game language and wraps to your active font.

This manual covers MyCinema 0.1.0 with pinned official WaterFrames, WaterMedia and WaterMedia Binaries. MyCinema owns the cinema, programme, schedule, projector-group and permission behavior. Back up your world before updating and inspect important cinemas in an independent copy.

Command/datapack lights in an existing map are not connected automatically; scene outputs need real wiring.

The chapters cover the film library, ordered programmes, halls, playback, schedules, information screens, posters, seats and staff access. A release candidate is automatically checked through source tests, 241 GameTests, dedicated-server runs, a native client and real movie playback.
mycinema.manual.chapter.install.title: 1. Matching versions
mycinema.manual.chapter.install.body:
Use the same pinned versions on client and server:

Minecraft 1.21.1
NeoForge 21.1.244
Java 21
MyCinema 0.1.0
WaterFrames 3.0.0-alpha.1
WaterMedia 3.0.0

The client also needs WaterMedia Binaries 3.0.0. WaterFrames includes WaterUI 1.0.0. The build resolves these official dependencies from Modrinth; MyCinema does not bundle or redistribute them.

Do not keep two versions of one mod in mods/. This open-source migration branch has not yet passed the full native QA suite.

Keep the pre-upgrade world, configuration and previous exact JAR set together. Rollback restores the world and matching JAR/configuration set; do not downgrade only the JAR on a migrated save.
mycinema.manual.chapter.register.title: 2. Register a hall
mycinema.manual.chapter.register.body:
Place the Control Terminal; its placer becomes its owner.

1. Right-click it with the Linking Card.
2. Right-click this hall's TMS with the card. This registers and selects the hall.
3. With that hall selected, right-click its outputs and information panel from within 8 blocks.

Shift-right-click the Control Terminal to cycle the card's hall. Right-clicking it normally selects the first hall. Read the hall name before binding.

The screen's hall arrows do NOT change the card selection. Output type selects the light group. One TMS can belong to only one Control Terminal. You need permission and loaded devices in the same dimension.
mycinema.manual.chapter.tablet.title: 3. Bind the tablet
mycinema.manual.chapter.tablet.body:
Within 8 blocks and with manager permission, hold the existing MyCinema Tablet and shift-right-click the Control Terminal. The server activates it for your player UUID, this controller's identity, owner and position, and this dimension.

Carry the activated tablet in your inventory or offhand and normally right-click a paired MyCinema staff door in this cinema, within normal interaction reach. You can hold an ordinary item; no tablet in hand or reader swipe is needed. Walking near a door does not open it. Newly paired doors in this cinema are covered too. Dropped items, chests and nested containers do not count.

Right-click the held tablet in the air to open remote controls. Remote emergency access also requires a current server-registered activation held in either hand and the same loaded controller. A saved media binding alone does not authorize emergency access. Door access does not grant media permissions.

Shift-right-click in the air to unbind and revoke this activation and its copies. Activating another tablet for the same player and cinema replaces the old activation. A pre-version tablet with a valid matching server registration upgrades on a valid door click. An old binding without a valid server grant must be reactivated at the authorized terminal.

Each click rechecks the real player, carried token, supported authorization version, current manager permission and exact controller identity, owner, position and dimension. No cross-cinema or cross-dimension entry. The reader, terminal and complete paired door must be current and loaded; no chunks are force-loaded. Revoked, copied-to-another-player, replaced-controller or changed-owner credentials cannot inherit authority. Employees still swipe their own cards at matching reader types.
mycinema.manual.chapter.sources.title: 4. Choose media
mycinema.manual.chapter.sources.body:
Right-click the TMS and open Sources in WaterFrames.

Enter an allowed media URL and add it, or use the local-media picker. Click the added row's thumbnail or title to select it. Selection changes the active source immediately.

Check ownership, media-saving permission and the server whitelist if rejected.

A local file: URI does not upload a video. Every viewing client needs that file at its own usable path, or use a URL every client can reach. Local paths are not guaranteed portable between Windows, macOS and Linux.
mycinema.manual.chapter.projection.title: 5. Projection Group
mycinema.manual.chapter.projection.body:
The official WaterFrames Standard Projector keeps its standalone behavior. MyCinema separately registers mycinema:cinema_projector and mycinema:imax_gt_projector as parallel devices. Each has its own item, block ID, cabinet model, inventory model, and recipe; neither depends on style fields or artwork from a private WaterFrames build.

Place either cabinet on a solid floor with clearance for the complete shape. IMAX GT measures about 1.625 × 1.4 × 2.48125 blocks and uses one visible functional anchor plus 17 invisible owned part cells. Collision is generated from the actual cabinet cuboids rather than a solid invisible 3 × 2 × 3 wall. Placement checks the whole footprint, loaded chunks, world bounds, floor support, and blocking entities before consuming an item.

The cabinet remains visible without media. Targeting or breaking any part resolves to the same device. Pick-block and drops retain the device type but never owner, binding, or media data. Breaking any part removes the complete machine and returns exactly one correct projector item in survival. Projector styles or model_core blocks from a historical private dependency are not silently rewritten in place; copy the world first and use the compatibility migration procedure to move them to the new MyCinema IDs.

At the TMS, open Projection Group and verify the intended pair before binding. Discovery reaches 16 blocks; local control requires device permission within 8 blocks. A group has at most two projectors, one media player, and one movie audio source. Binding enables Linked Controls by default.

Controls on a directly opened linked projector are disabled; adjust it through the TMS. A missing or unloaded TMS keeps the lock. Unlink only for deliberate per-device geometry calibration. Release verification must cover both independent IDs, the complete IMAX GT structure, asset loading, real movie playback, and a dedicated client screenshot of the cabinet.
mycinema.manual.chapter.linked.title: 6. Linked Controls
mycinema.manual.chapter.linked.body:
Leave Linked Controls enabled for matched-pair adjustments through the TMS.

World X/Y/Z movement applies the same delta to both projectors, preserving their alignment difference. Width, height, rotation and projection distance apply the requested shared value. Unchanged properties are not copied.

Use Unlink Controls at the TMS only when deliberately calibrating one projector. Choose the correct member, make the adjustment, then re-enable Linked Controls for normal operation.

Unlinking control scope does not unbind the projectors or create separate media players. After unlinking controls, you may also open a projector directly to edit its geometry with its owner permission within 8 blocks. Media and audio remain on the TMS. Check both images after every calibration change.
mycinema.manual.chapter.geometry.title: 7. Screen geometry
mycinema.manual.chapter.geometry.body:
Adjust the image from the TMS. Choose a 0.01, 0.1 or 1 block movement step.

Screen up/down changes the image's world Y position. Higher Y moves the whole image upward. Width and height resize it. Projection distance moves it forward/back along the projection direction; rotation turns the image.

Keep calibrated width, height and projection distance when correcting only vertical alignment. Linked Controls applies matching deltas to the pair.

The earlier 42 x 23.625 block test image was a QA example, not the required size for GT, Wide or every hall. Use the actual screen's measured geometry.
mycinema.manual.chapter.limits.title: 8. A 40-block cap?
mycinema.manual.chapter.limits.body:
The matching WaterFrames source defaults display width and height limits to 64 blocks. Existing saved server configuration can still retain a 40-block cap.

Stop and back up the world before changing its active server configuration:
<world>/serverconfig/waterframes-server.toml

Under [waterframes.rendering], set maxWidth = 64.0 and maxHeight = 64.0, then restart. In singleplayer the world is under saves/.

These values are limits, not screen dimensions. Raising them does not resize a calibrated screen. Render distance and projection distance are separate controls.
mycinema.manual.chapter.audio.title: 9. Audio range
mycinema.manual.chapter.audio.body:
Full-volume Radius is the distance without attenuation. Audible Range is the outer reach. Sound fades between these radii; equal radii produce a cutoff instead of a fade. New TMS devices start at a 64-block full-volume radius, capped by the server. Existing devices retain their saved values.

Open the TMS Audio origin tab to choose the position of its one movie audio source:

Projector position: the midpoint of both bound projector block centers. This is the default for new and old saves.

Screen center: the center of the two actual projected image faces. Their rectangles must align within 0.25 blocks. World offsets, dimensions, rotation, anchor and projection distance are included, so this point follows later calibration. Misaligned screens make this mode silent.

Audience center: enter a real world X/Y/Z and Save audience center. Saving does not select the mode; then choose Audience center. Until calibrated, it is silent. The point must be within the displayed server limit, the world border/build height and an already loaded chunk.

All modes need the current two loaded, reciprocally linked projector identities. Missing or replaced devices, unavailable origins and unloaded origin chunks produce silence with a status explanation. There is no guessed fallback or forced chunk load.

Change origins locally at the TMS with ownership/authorization for both members, within 8 blocks. Origin selection keeps the same decoder, clock, mute and volume; it creates no additional speaker or audio stream. The full-volume/audible radii use the selected origin, not a wall-aware hall boundary. Legacy audio offsets do not select these presets.

Cloud tests use Null OpenAL. Verified engine state does not prove heard positioning or audio quality on real speakers. No room-acoustic simulation, DCI/DCP or KDM support is claimed.
mycinema.manual.chapter.playback.title: 10. Run a show
mycinema.manual.chapter.playback.body:
Open the Control Terminal or bound tablet. Select the hall and check All / Hall before issuing a scene.

Load a title and allowed media URL into the selected hall; loading leaves it paused. Admission prepares entry. Play starts the feature; Pause pauses it; Stop ends playback for departure; Close stops and marks the venue closed.

Scenes apply light presets and admission-door hold output. Venue-open status is separate from door hold and actual wired output.

Manual scenes, lights or door actions take over the hall. Resume automatic permits future schedules; it does not replay a show already overridden.

In the Control Terminal, Stop / Exit also disables the recorded, loaded projector outputs after the stop acknowledgement. The cabinet and TMS links remain. Pause and the 3-second inter-clip black interval do not power them off. A later explicitly loaded or scheduled programme enables them again. Stop remains available after programme completion. The locked WaterFrames TMS/playlist-detail UI still restricts its own Stop button after completion; use the Control Terminal departure control for this case.

In the Control page, scroll over the lower lighting shortcuts and typed-media area to reach its remaining controls. Seek, admission, playback Stop / Exit, emergency access, status and Done stay visible. Devices, Information and Lighting scroll their central content. The schedule editor scrolls its fields while Review save and Back remain visible.

Programme chunk recovery: while the enrolled TMS chunk is unavailable, keep the saved ordered programme and last confirmed clip position, pause/play intent and unconsumed transition gap. The manager reports that it is waiting; unavailable time does not advance the programme. Public current-programme posters are withheld until the live association is verified again.

A returning terminal must be the same enrolled identity with a genuinely replaced block entity, unchanged prior session/source/evidence, current owner/controller grant and current local-source consent. Only then does recovery use the existing paused prepare and fresh viewer Ready path. Same-instance epoch changes or another source remain a takeover, never an automatic rebind. Finished history does not restart.

An authorized Stop or scheduled cancellation while the terminal is unavailable is retained as pending, including across saves. It is applied before any resume after the target is loaded and authority is checked. Waiting for stop is not an acknowledgement that media already stopped. Never rely on an unloaded target for an immediate action. Keep the separate release report for the exact tested scope.
mycinema.manual.chapter.seek.title: 11. Timeline control
mycinema.manual.chapter.seek.body:
Use the timeline for the currently selected single hall. The server must know a trustworthy duration and accept the current media session.

Drag to preview a target, then release to request one seek. Wait for confirmation before another request. The server rechecks the hall, permissions, source and session; stale requests are rejected.

Changing halls, sources or control scope cancels an unfinished drag. Live media, unknown duration, unavailable devices and All Halls do not provide a usable seek control.

Seeking within a clip keeps the existing playback state; seeking to its end pauses there. A successful seek takes manual control of this hall while retaining the current programme identity. Use Resume automatic to permit future scheduled shows. It does not replay an overridden show. Request cooldown and media-frame rounding still apply; arbitrary files do not gain guaranteed frame-accurate positioning.

New programmes use an explicit ordered playlist. The progress bar controls only the current clip; dragging to its end pauses there. Use Playlist → Previous, Next or Choose to switch clips. Repeated occurrences remain separate. Each switch to another clip uses a 3-second black and silent interval, then prepares the next clip under black until Ready. Pausing freezes the remaining interval; offline time never consumes it. There is no leading or trailing configured interval, and a single clip has none. Programme total includes the (clip count − 1) intervals; trusted media lengths remain unchanged.

TMS and manager read the same complete programme view. Stop/cancel retains the list as history and never deletes the library. Reload the complete film explicitly from the library to start again at its first clip. Native playlist/loop autosaves cannot overwrite a managed programme. Same-programme control retains its current scheduled identity; replacing the source remains an explicit takeover. Existing saved snapshots retain their legacy timing; new loads/new schedules use the new 3-second policy. Replacing a future plan is explicit and does not alter an old plan silently.
mycinema.manual.chapter.schedule.title: 12. Save a schedule
mycinema.manual.chapter.schedule.body:
Open Schedule. Save the intended time zone, then select a hall. Use the current-hall/all-halls filter and page controls to browse every show. Select a row by its stable show identity.

Film Library opens reusable films and ordered programmes while keeping this hall and selected show. See the Film Library chapter for metadata, immutable snapshots and programme controls.

New opens the existing single-source form. Edit changes only a future pending show. Review title, source, local start time and planned minutes before confirming. The row keeps its identity when time changes. Another operator changing the manager rejects a stale save instead of overwriting it.

Load saved show reuses the selected server-stored source without typing it again. Control also displays that selected title and source, labelled with its hall. Loading replaces current media, pauses at the beginning and takes manual control. It preserves the future plan; Resume automatic before future scheduled starts.

Cancel keeps the record. For an active show its confirmation explicitly stops playback and takes manual control. Delete removes an inactive record after confirmation; active records must first be stopped and cancelled. History cannot be edited into a new show.

Saving is not enabling. In the single-source form, planned minutes define the schedule end, not measured movie duration. Film Library plans instead derive their end from the recorded whole-film runtime. Past starts, overlaps, invalid local times and stale revisions are rejected.

Film Library programmes use a planned end and finish naturally; source-ready delays are shown in management, and conflicting successors are missed explicitly. See Film Library for this separate rule.
mycinema.manual.chapter.automatic.title: 13. Enable automation
mycinema.manual.chapter.automatic.body:
Select a future pending show and choose Prepare scheduled start. Confirm that scheduling will be enabled and this hall returned to automatic control. The server verifies its owner, current TMS enrollment and source permission. Other halls keep their control modes. The film does not load or start immediately.

Load for inspection is a different action: it loads paused and takes manual control. After checking the source, use Prepare scheduled start again if timed playback is wanted. Lighting, door scenes, playback and seeking also take manual control.

The first due tick either starts the show or records why it is Missed. The 30-second allowance is for a late first tick, not a retry queue. Disabled scheduling, manual override or a previous unconfirmed stop can immediately mark it Missed. Details retains the reason. A paused single-player server does not tick. No chunks are forced to load.

A missed show never replays automatically. Restore permissions/devices and create a future plan, or load it manually. Starting/stopping media failures appear as Failed or Waiting to Stop; a later show blocked by an unconfirmed stop does not silently catch up.
mycinema.manual.chapter.lights.title: 14. Lights and doors
mycinema.manual.chapter.lights.body:
MyCinema outputs redstone for MAIN, AISLE, EXIT, ACCENT and admission-door hold. Wire the correct output to a new circuit, then bind it with the hall-selected card.

Each hall stores Admission, Ads / Trailers, Feature, Pause, Exit and Cleaning presets. All four light groups allow 0-15; 0 turns that output off. Save a preset, then apply it. Vanilla redstone lamps are on/off, not dimmable.

Keep emergency exits independently usable. Admission hold is not a security lock.

Current map command/datapack lights are NOT connected. Its eight restored end rods remain fixed lights, not scene-controlled fixtures. Final map integration remains a separate task.
mycinema.manual.chapter.information.body:
Hall guest screens show a poster, human-entered film title, HH:mm–HH:mm and runtime, without a Today prefix for the current day. Lobby programme dates retain their day context. No file path, full timestamp, seconds, playback status or setup diagnostics are shown. Tomorrow or MM-dd identifies future dates; an end after midnight says next day. Lobby programmes additionally identify the hall and paginate every eligible planned row.

Scheduled start and end use the manager's explicit timezone internally. Runtime is separately trusted media duration; the scheduled slot length never substitutes for it. Unknown runtime is —. A manual duration override is labelled Runtime(manual), and never changes the trusted playback clock.

Empty Hall fields follow the verified programme actually loaded for this hall, then an eligible current/next plan when no programme remains. A manual film load displays No scheduled time; its title, runtime and poster still come from the same saved film. Explicit Hall overrides still display with no plan. Standalone manual mode needs no controller and saving it unbinds only this screen. Lobby mode ignores manual overrides. The time and runtime visibility switches must be enabled. Missed/failed/ended shows are not an automatic active listing.

Right-click opens the read-only visitor view; Shift-right-click opens the owner editor. Public snapshots refresh about every two seconds. Overflow pages rotate and retain complete rows. Details and error diagnostics stay in management screens.

Automatic auditorium schedule means this screen follows one explicitly bound hall. The hall-name override edits display text; it does not select a hall. Save that mode, use the Cinema Linking Card on the controller, then the intended TMS, then the screen. Sneak-use the card on the controller to cycle an already registered hall; read the selected name. The owner editor shows actual binding and schedule status. For an automatic film poster, leave the screen override blank and choose poster-above/beside. A film poster changed after scheduling does not rewrite that immutable saved show. Automatic poster loading diagnostics now report the real published source state; the visitor view also displays an approved poster in poster layouts.

The Layout page has separate Film, Show time and Runtime header switches: turning a header off keeps its value visible. Whole-field visibility remains separate. Matching poster images can share one texture after each panel is independently authorized. Four different images can be cached together; a further distinct image reports capacity instead of remaining silently blank. Changed image bytes at one URL cannot borrow an older panel’s pixels.

Poster visibility still depends on the chosen layout: TEXT intentionally has no image. Choose a poster layout for a film poster. An explicitly entered panel poster overrides inheritance. Automatic film inheritance applies to a bound auditorium, not a lobby list. The owner Pictures page distinguishes no programme, empty saved poster, local-unpublished and denied publication.
mycinema.manual.chapter.music.title: 16. Background music
mycinema.manual.chapter.music.body:
The matching WaterFrames build temporarily suppresses this client's Minecraft MUSIC category while a loaded, tracked TMS is actively playing inside its audible range.

It stops current MUSIC and blocks new MUSIC starts. It does not edit your saved Music volume, mute film audio/RECORDS or silence every sound category. Other mods using MUSIC are included; custom categories are not.

The hold ends after every relevant hall pauses, stops, disappears or moves out of range. Multiple nearby halls keep the hold until all release it. Normal music selection can then resume; the old track is not resumed at the same timestamp.

This is client range detection, not a map-wide BGM command adapter.
mycinema.manual.chapter.limits_and_statu:
Verify the exact integrated set in an independent world copy first: loaded devices and permission, full-model placement and parts, TMS linking and audio origin, both projected images, timeline, a future schedule and its stop, a wired circuit, and a wall information panel.

For access, check a manager's normal door click while carrying an activated tablet and holding an ordinary item; walking nearby must not open it. Check ENTRY/SERVICE cards at several matching readers, replacement and revoke, four reader facings and legacy bindings, then emergency unlock, explicit restore and save/reload with loaded and unloaded door regions.

The public release verification separates compilation, model checks, GameTests, dedicated-server restart, native English/Chinese menus, visible movie playback, save/reload and audio-device opening. Run ./gradlew verifyRelease and inspect build/release-evidence for the recorded results. A headless result does not prove graphics or audible output.

An existing cinema map's command lights are not connected automatically. Wire MyCinema's redstone outputs to the intended circuits and verify them in a world copy. MyCinema does not automatically install or migrate a map, simulate room acoustics, or claim DCI/DCP/KDM compatibility.

Before removing a Manager Terminal or changing a map, confirm active shows have stopped and back up the world. Keep the previous exact JAR set, configuration and pre-upgrade world together. Roll back that world and its matching JAR/configuration set as a pair; replacing only the JAR on a migrated world is not a validated downgrade.

mycinema.panel.hint: Shift-right-click an owned panel to edit. Changes apply to its loaded joined screen.

mycinema.manual.chapter.panels.title: Wall information panels
mycinema.manual.chapter.panels.body:
Place an Information Panel against a solid block’s side for a thin wall panel; floor placement keeps the original cube. Every segment needs its own backing. Same-owner, same-facing segments with equal settings and bindings merge across left/right/up/down into filled rectangular screens. Defaults are 16 blocks per axis and 256 blocks per screen; mycinema-displays-server.toml can raise this to at most 32 per axis and 1024 blocks. Every segment needs backing. Holes split the screen into complete rectangles; oversized connected components become separate tiles. Only loaded chunks participate. Removing a segment repartitions the screen; surviving tiles retain their settings.

Empty-hand Shift-right-click opens the owner/administrator editor. Choose Standalone manual, Hall information or Lobby programme, then save. Standalone needs no controller; saving it unbinds only this screen without changing schedules. Hall mode binds to the card-selected hall. Lobby mode uses the card-selected manager and lists its halls only; no selected hall is required. Changing back from Lobby requires binding a hall again. Binding requires current panel and manager permission in the same dimension and loaded chunks.

Hall mode first shows the verified programme actually loaded by its bound TMS. When no actual programme remains, it shows an eligible current or next planned show. While a current programme is restoring or its current authorization or playback-session checks fail, it waits instead of substituting an unrelated future film. In schedule-fallback mode, the guest viewer can also list later planned shows; an actual programme supplies its own single row. Hall title, hall name and show-time overrides are display-only customization; existing values survive upgrades. They can label an unscheduled presentation even when no programme or schedule row exists. Without a verified programme or eligible planned row, automatic stale titles are never revived and unknown values are —. A verified manually loaded film supplies its saved title, runtime and poster and displays No scheduled time; a separate display title is optional. Lobby ignores these overrides and never invents schedule entries. A manual duration text override is labelled by default and never changes the media clock. Legacy status, next-show and footer text is never public.

Text, poster-above and poster-beside layouts retain colours, text size and visibility switches. Hall screens show film, time range and runtime; the hall label applies only to Lobby. Poster and text occupy separate areas. Increasing height fits more lines. Long rows continue across measured pages instead of being cut off. The guest viewer preserves its page number on refresh and clamps it if the programme shrinks. Saves apply to the complete loaded rectangle; changed membership, ownership or settings require Reload saved first. Reload discards the draft.

Posters accept real PNG, JPEG and WebP content, including extensionless CDN URLs with query strings. Source width and height may each be 1–8192 pixels; any aspect ratio is allowed. The complete image fits without stretching or cropping. PNG/JPEG use header-checked subsampling; WebP uses bounded WaterMedia still-image decoding. No movie player or audio track is created. Animated inputs show the first image/frame.

The old fixed 8 MiB input limit is removed. Client config mycinema-client.toml exposes downloadBudgetMiB (default 64, range 16–256), decodeBudgetMiB (256, range 64–768), textureMaxSide (2048, range 512–8192) and textureBudgetMiB (16, range 4–64). Decode also respects one third of the JVM heap and currently available memory with a reserve. Large lossless WebP may exceed this working budget even within 8192 axes. PNG/JPEG can be sampled before full-size allocation. Textures shrink proportionally to the configured edge/pixel budget and actual GPU limit; accepted source dimensions are separate from displayed resolution. At most four textures are cached.

HTTP(S) allows at most five redirects within a 30-second whole request, with five-second I/O deadlines. Every target is checked against current server policy and the saved author grant. Redirects to localhost/private/reserved addresses, HTTPS downgrade, credentials and loops are rejected; no cookies or authorization headers are sent. An explicitly approved direct LAN URL remains usable, but redirect targets must be public. Each viewer needs any local file on their own computer. The owner editor reports precise saved-source failures and provides Retry saved poster. Visitor walls show no private error details. Unsaved draft text is not fetched. Cached final destinations are reauthorized every two seconds.

Existing map command lights remain a separate integration task. Redstone outputs still require actual wiring.

An administrator or an author with the server's explicit save and whitelist-bypass permissions may save a poster outside the domain list. Its server-only authorization records the real author, exact source and panel ownership. The server rechecks current permissions after load and every two seconds; revoked bypass hides an otherwise blocked poster. Regular players still follow the whitelist. Legacy posters without such a record need an authorized re-save if outside the whitelist.

Known codec limit: the current WaterMedia lossless WebP decoder rejects some constant-fill images above 16,777,216 pixels even if the configured memory budget is sufficient. This is reported as a codec limit, not as a corrupt file; export PNG/JPEG for those cases.

The input budget is also reduced when needed to fit one sixth of the JVM heap and one third of available heap after a 32 MiB reserve. Memory-based refusal is labelled separately from the configured download size limit. Containers are limited to 4,096 chunks/segments and source references to 2,048 characters.

On the Layout page, Visible fields switches control complete rows. The separate Field headers switches control only the Film, Show time and Runtime labels, including the manually entered runtime label. Turn off a header to retain its value without the label or colon. These choices apply to the physical screen and guest viewer, for manual text and automatic programme data. New and older panels keep all headers on until changed; save to apply. The Lobby hall label is unchanged.

Per-entry display layout: select Text group, Title, Showtime, Runtime, Format, Hall or Poster. Choose left/center/right and top/middle/bottom, then X/Y offsets. Offsets are thousandths of that entry area: 100 means10%, not device pixels. Automatic flow/reset restores the old sequential layout; explicit anchors can intentionally overlap within a programme, so review both world surface and guest view. Poster share and position are independent of text. The Format field is display text such as IMAX GT,2D or3D; it never changes playback or projector mode. Header switches hide labels while values remain; separate visibility controls can hide fields.

Operations role uses the existing Information Panel item and block IDs. In its owner editor choose Screen role: Operations, keep Hall or Lobby scope, save, and bind with your manager card. A Hall binding remains selected when switching roles. Standalone manual has no operations role. Colours and text size apply to the operations wall; its structured rows use their own full-width layout. Saved audience poster, overrides and layout remain available when you switch back.

The wall shows source-free current programme/clip totals and today’s planned shows in the cinema time zone, including shows crossing midnight. Right-click opens Programme / playlist and Today’s schedule. Only the actual owner of both screen and cinema can use this console. An OP, creative inventory, staff door card, copied block or client role field does not grant playback control. Delegated staff operation is not enabled in this release.

Commands reuse the existing manager playback and load-show services, including TMS ownership, automation grant, current run/revision/clip, source policy and local-media consent checks. Stay within 8 blocks of the screen. Remote manager control additionally requires its currently activated and registered tablet; otherwise stay within 8 blocks of the manager. The console does not issue grants, enable local media or edit schedules. It adds no separate lighting controls; playback keeps the existing stage-light behavior. Programme view lists the actual loaded clip sequence; the schedule tab lists plans separately. Loading a pending show for today needs an explicit confirmation and may replace the current programme.

The server rechecks identity, owner, binding, hall scope, group revision and permissions on every request. Changed ownership, role, unloaded/replaced blocks or revoked tablet/media authority disable the next request. Unknown/newer role data is retained and locked until an explicit valid save. New placements cannot inherit saved ownership or command authority from copied item data. Updates refresh every two seconds; a command without a reply is never automatically replayed. Reopen or refresh to check the real state. The repository verifyRelease task automatically checks source compilation, isolated-server behavior and native-client acceptance.

The current screening poster remains through opening, admission, lighting and play/pause changes. It stays after natural completion until an explicit Stop/Close or a new programme replaces it; the panel then shows the next eligible scheduled screening or idle state. This retention is display-only and never restarts media. Invalid ownership, controller, source or authorization withholds publication. Old completed history does not automatically become a current display.

mycinema.manual.chapter.advertising.body:
Place an LED Advertising Panel or Printed Sign on a solid block's side for a wall mount, or on its top for a floor sign. LED pixels are visually full-bright; they do not emit Minecraft block light. Printed signs use the surrounding world light. Picture mode shows still images; Information uses MyCinema public fields. LED Borrowed media draws an existing WaterFrames texture without another player or audio track. A floor sign has a thin physical body and a shallow foot. The collision follows those parts, not the empty bounding box around them.

Right-click a sign or one of its occupied segments as its owner to open Picture Display. Choose a local file, enter an allowed URL/resource, or use Upload to game server. Local choice and real upload are separate actions. Apply image source saves the image. Clear image removes the displayed reference without deleting a shared server asset.

Expand or shrink the left, right, top or bottom edge. Switch the adjustment step between 0.125 m and 1 m. Apply physical size commits the draft. Draft 1 × 1 m changes only the size draft until applied. Images always fit proportionally without cropping. The original anchor must stay within the sign; one axis is limited to 16 m or a smaller configured server cap. Fractional offsets may occupy up to 17 × 17 block cells even though the body is at most 16 × 16 m.

Expansion needs empty, loaded cells, current edit permission, and backing for wall signs or sturdy ground or a valid matching standing-board support chain beneath the floor sign's base. It never loads chunks or replaces another block. A support, ownership or structure change can reject the operation. Reload saved discards the editor draft. Breaking the root or a linked segment removes the linked sign; block protection remains the server's responsibility. Save and test your layout before installing many signs.

To combine small units, place matching owned 1 m panels into a filled rectangle, then choose Assemble matching units and confirm the displayed count. Content, mode, facing, support and ownership must match. Breaking the assembled sign returns the consumed number of units, even after resizing. Standing units can form horizontal rows or vertical columns. Hold sneak and use a matching printed sign or LED item on the top edge of your own standing board. The new unit keeps its facing but stays independent; it does not copy media or merge automatically. Two or three units can then be explicitly assembled into one continuous image with one bottom foot.

Apply uploaded PNG silhouette uses a private server upload only. A maximum 32×32 conservative outer grid and 128 merged body boxes approximate the opaque pixels; the independent floor foot stays solid. The silhouette worker accepts static noninterlaced PNG up to 16,777,216 pixels and 8192 per side. Unsupported/interlaced/animated, fully transparent or client-only images keep rectangular collision. This is a silhouette-processing budget, not a new 16M-pixel limit on displaying posters. If the image is loading, revoked or failed, neutral silhouette material remains visible so collision does not disappear visually.

Wall-mounted printed signs and LEDs can continue upward or downward by placing a matching unit against the top/bottom edge of an existing wall unit or its linked segment. The new unit keeps that wall facing and still needs solid backing at its own cell; it is independently owned and does not copy media or merge automatically. Use Assemble matching units explicitly for a complete matching rectangle. Each stacked standing unit requires a loaded, live support chain of the same material, facing and owner down to sturdy ground. Its full bottom width must meet a rectangular supporting top exactly, with no fractional-height gap. A silhouette-shaped separate board cannot support another unit; apply the private PNG silhouette after merging the grounded whole sign instead. Missing, replaced, differently owned, misaligned or unloaded support rejects new placement without consuming an item. Removing a lower board or ground, or resizing/changing it so contact is lost, removes unsupported upper signs and their linked parts through normal support validation; assembled signs return their original unit counts. Unloaded existing support is deferred without loading chunks. The size editor still supports 0.125 m steps; Apply physical size saves them. Extending Bottom into the ground remains blocked.
mycinema.manual.chapter.picture_transfer:
Choose local image stores a file URI only. It does not upload any bytes. Every viewing computer needs the same file path, and the saved reference can disclose that path. Use this for a private single-player installation or deliberately synchronized client media.

Upload to game server opens the file chooser, checks the image, then asks before transmission. Dropping a file onto an image editor selects it for the same confirmed upload flow. The confirmation names the file and byte count locally and explains server disk and viewer bandwidth. Only image bytes and an opaque content hash go to the current game server; the local path and filename are not transmitted. No external image host or public cloud upload is involved.

The server stores images inside the world in mycinema-panel-assets-v1. Back up that directory with the world. Default asset limits are 64 MiB per image, 512 MiB per world and 4096 images. mycinema-assets-server.toml exposes per-image and per-world budgets. The per-image hard ceiling is 256 MiB. The existing viewer input/decode/texture budgets still apply separately. Uploading successfully does not promise that every client's memory or GPU can display the original at full resolution.

Images use 32 KiB chunks with acknowledgments. Limits are one upload per player, four server uploads, one download per viewer and eight server downloads. Uploads accept at most two chunks per tick per uploader; downloads send at most one chunk per tick per viewer. Idle transfers expire after 15 seconds and any transfer after 15 minutes. Identical image bytes deduplicate storage, but another owner must still upload/prove possession before authoring that asset onto their own sign. Guessing a hash grants no authority.

Only the display owner or existing authorized administrator can upload through its editor. Authority, identity, group membership and loaded range are checked throughout. A viewer can fetch only a currently approved image from a nearby display, within 64 blocks of its surface. Revoked or replaced bindings stop new transfers. Do not treat this as DRM: a viewer who already received image bytes can retain them.

PNG, JPEG and WebP use real container checks; filename extensions are not trusted. Each source axis is at most 8192 pixels, with no aspect-ratio restriction. The server validates the stream without a full image allocation. The client still performs the budgeted real decode and reports unsupported or damaged content. Completed images are immutable and remain stored when a panel is removed; they are not automatically deleted. Failed or cancelled staging transfers are cleaned up and remain accounted for until removal succeeds.

mycinema.manual.chapter.film_library.bod:
Open Film Library on the Control Terminal’s Schedule page. The selected hall and show are carried into the library; Done returns to the same manager selection. The library holds at most 64 films and each film holds 1–16 ordered source segments. Repeated sources are intentional and retain their positions. These are ordinary media sources, not a cinema-package import format.

First ownership registration for a legacy map: manual playback does not prove that the TMS has a recorded owner. Media sources and duration shows the selected hall’s saved programme grant and local-source consent. If the TMS is explicitly unowned and both reciprocally bound projectors are also unowned, the actual Control Terminal owner may choose Claim this unowned hall while within 8 blocks of that Control Terminal and holding current level-4 operator permission. Review the exact TMS, projector and controller identities in the confirmation. Only this matching, loaded group in the same dimension can be claimed. Existing or mixed ownership, replaced devices, changed bindings and stale confirmations are rejected; this cannot transfer someone else’s devices.

Claiming stops playback at zero and puts the hall in manual mode while preserving media addresses, playlist, original save author, geometry, volume and calibration. Pending plans remain; any running show becomes manually overridden. Old playback leases, current duration facts and previous local-source consents for this hall are retired. Revalidate media for fresh evidence from the current owner, then separately confirm programme control and any required local-source consent. Claiming starts no playback, grants neither consent and does not enable the scheduler. Do not substitute broad map-install or repair functions for this explicitly selected-hall workflow. After a programme grant is saved, later automatic operation does not require the owner to remain within 8 blocks; loaded devices, current server permissions and viewer Ready are still required.

New film and Edit film let you save a display title, an optional authorized poster reference, and the ordered sources. Select a numbered row to edit its source. Add, duplicate, remove or move a segment, then Save film. Film and plan selections use stable IDs, with expected revisions checked on the server. A conflict preserves the draft and requires Reload; Reload explicitly discards that page’s draft. Delete film asks for confirmation and keeps existing scheduled snapshots intact. A local poster path stays private and is not automatically sent to guest panels; use an approved image URL or upload through a panel editor and reuse that server asset reference.

Sources & length is for inspection. Select a hall and segment, then confirm Prepare selected source. This replaces that hall’s current media, uses source 0 for the selected URL, pauses at the beginning and takes manual control. The visible segment numbering starts at 1; it is separate from the media source selector 0. Preparing one segment does not load the whole programme. Read selected length inspects the matching current source without changing playback. Repeated occurrences of the exact source share its accepted observation.

Validate all sources checks each unique source once in a serial paused queue, clearing old library metadata and allowing up to 30 seconds per source for a fresh report from the online owner’s viewing client; the server does not decode media. A failure stops the queue, and a single-source preparation, film edit or film deletion cancels it. Existing planned snapshots are unchanged and no playback starts.

Viewer Ready means a tracked client has opened the current source and reports Paused or Playing; that viewer need not be the owner and cannot supply trusted length just by being ready. Recording a library length has a separate owner-evidence requirement for the exact source and media session. The server saves a historical owner report tied to its evidence, controller and terminal identities. It is not permanent certification of a URL’s bytes, content, availability or future duration. A saved runtime is not proof that the hall is currently ready. Unknown lengths stay Unknown; live sources have no finite film runtime. Runtime is calculated from accepted segment lengths, including repeated segments, never typed into the library form.

When the server reports whole-programme support and every segment has a finite accepted length, confirm Load programme paused. It copies the film revision into a programme snapshot, replaces current media, pauses at the beginning and takes manual control. It does not autoplay. Later automatic segment changes require the TMS owner’s existing local controller authorization; the load action does not create a grant. For a missing grant, the actual owner must stand within 8 blocks of the Control Terminal and separately confirm Authorize programme control for the selected hall. This persistent grant identifies the exact controller and TMS and permits programme control while the owner is offline. It does not start playback or enable the global scheduler. Current server media permissions remain required; manual administrator loading alone does not authorize delegated programme playback. Local sources blocked by domain-whitelist policy require the separate film-scoped consent described below. An accepted load may still be Preparing; it is not proof of Ready or Playing. Open hall controls selects this exact hall with All halls off; use Play, Pause, Stop and the timeline there. Unsaved library drafts require confirmation before leaving. Single-source inspection remains available when programme support is unavailable.

Local-source consent is a separate optional second step. First confirm Authorize programme control for the selected hall. If local sources are blocked by the web-domain whitelist, the actual owner must stand within 8 blocks of the Control Terminal and confirm Authorize this film’s local sources. Scroll through the exact film ID/revision, controller, TMS and ordered normalized sources before confirming. The server saves consent for that film revision and its accepted source evidence only; another film, revision, source order, evidence or TMS needs its own matching consent. At most 128 grants and 1 MiB of consent data are retained per controller.

Consent cannot override ordinary server saving, game-mode or control restrictions. Current administrator-level or explicit save-and-bypass eligibility is rechecked for every source operation; losing that eligibility blocks consent-dependent playback. HTTP(S) domain rules stay unchanged. Consent does not start playback, enable the global scheduler or create the ordinary programme grant.

Revoke local-source consent clears all film-revision consents for the selected hall and immediately pauses playback that depends on them. Pending programmes cannot use revoked consent. Independently allowed local sources still follow current server policy; ordinary programme authorization and scheduler settings remain separate. Only the actual owner can revoke, including through a valid bound Tablet.

A local path never uploads or synchronizes a video with the world. Every viewing client needs its own readable file at the named local path. Relative paths such as media/feature.mkv and media/bonus.mkv resolve on each client; repeated segments retain their separate positions and contribute their duration again. Neither consent nor accepted duration proves identical file contents across clients.

Schedule film lets you choose the hall and local start time in the controller’s saved time zone. The end comes from the complete recorded runtime. Creating a plan copies an immutable film revision and source order; subsequent library edits, reordering and deletion do not rewrite that plan. To change its media, explicitly select a future pending plan and confirm Replace selected plan with this film. Change selected plan’s time preserves its existing snapshot and runtime. Stale revisions, missing evidence, invalid times and overlaps are rejected.

Saving a plan does not enable the scheduler or release manual takeover. Return to Schedule and review Prepare scheduled start for the intended future plan. Ordered loading and scheduling controls follow the server’s advertised capability; a saved multi-source list alone does not mean ordered playback is available.

Check the exact release report for the tested client, server, UI and media scope. Results for one build or platform do not establish all-platform acceptance or audible sound quality.

Film Library schedules retain their original planned start and end. The end is a planning time, not a command to cut an unfinished film. Source preparation and viewer-Ready waits do not consume film runtime; only the final segment’s natural Ended event marks the programme Completed. If it is still active after the planned end, the manager shows a short delayed status and a full explanation. A later same-hall show that becomes due while this programme remains active is marked Missed with a conflict reason; neither film is silently replaced or rescheduled. Manual Stop or cancellation does not claim natural completion, and preparation/permission failures remain failures. A restored active programme still proves its saved lease, prepares paused and waits for new Ready at the saved position, even past the planned end. Guest panels retain the active film and its original planned time range; unknown trusted runtime remains unknown. Legacy single-source shows with a manually entered slot length retain their scheduled stop behavior.

After a world reload, a verified completed programme keeps its full total and Completed status as read-only history. It cannot resume or create playback authority; replacing the source retires this current summary while the completed schedule record remains.

New programmes use an explicit ordered playlist. The progress bar controls only the current clip; dragging to its end pauses there. Use Playlist → Previous, Next or Choose to switch clips. Repeated occurrences remain separate. Each switch to another clip uses a 3-second black and silent interval, then prepares the next clip under black until Ready. Pausing freezes the remaining interval; offline time never consumes it. There is no leading or trailing configured interval, and a single clip has none. Programme total includes the (clip count − 1) intervals; trusted media lengths remain unchanged.

TMS and manager read the same complete programme view. Stop/cancel retains the list as history and never deletes the library. Reload the complete film explicitly from the library to start again at its first clip. Native playlist/loop autosaves cannot overwrite a managed programme. Same-programme control retains its current scheduled identity; replacing the source remains an explicit takeover. Existing saved snapshots retain their legacy timing; new loads/new schedules use the new 3-second policy. Replacing a future plan is explicit and does not alter an old plan silently.

The bound hall display now selects its verified current programme before an upcoming plan. Film title, poster and timing come from the same immutable snapshot; a manual load has no scheduled time, so the screen says so instead of inventing one. Stop, cancellation, revoked ownership/session or an unrelated source cannot revive an old programme. A saved public poster stays pinned; explicitly reload the film or replace a future plan to select a different public poster. Missing or local-only saved posters have the narrow metadata-only fallback described below. The owner Pictures page explains no programme, empty or old poster snapshot, unpublishable local path, TEXT layout and current download/decode failures.

Local library posters: use Upload local poster, choose an image, review the server transmission, then save the film. Upload alone changes only the draft. Nearby viewers of approved information panels can receive the published image; local paths and filenames are not sent. A plain file path cannot be shared. No per-screen image registration is needed.

Saved public posters stay pinned. If a saved programme has no poster or only a private local poster, a newer authorized library poster can fill it only when film ID, title and every ordered segment/metadata record are exactly unchanged. This does not replace media, duration, consent or schedule. Deleted, changed or unauthorized library entries are not borrowed.

Catalog JSON exchange: on the Library page, choose Catalog JSON exchange. Choose a UTF-8 .json file to check it locally, select the ID conflict policy, then choose Send metadata for server preview. This sends its titles, poster references and ordered media paths to the current Minecraft server; it does not upload media or image files. Review every action and warning, then choose Review and import and explicitly confirm. Before final confirmation, closing or declining leaves the catalog unchanged. A changed catalog revision, owner, connection or controller requires a new preview; close and reopen the library after a conflict.

The portable schema is mycinema.catalog, version 1, at most 1 MiB of UTF-8 JSON, 64 films and 1–16 playlist clips per film. Each film has a canonical UUID id, title, poster, format and playlist; each clip has source and durationMs. Unknown or duplicate fields, malformed data, unsupported versions and known credential-bearing URL references are rejected. -1 means unknown duration; a positive duration up to seven days is only an unverified display hint. The format label (for example 2D or IMAX GT) does not change projector mode or certify a media package. Exact segment order and repeated occurrences are retained. This is not DCP/KDM import.

ID conflicts default to Skip. Copy gives the incoming film a new independent ID; Update keeps the existing ID and clears its trusted source observations. A deleted film ID retained by an existing show can only be skipped or copied. Preview changes nothing; confirmation rechecks current save permissions and catalog quotas and applies all accepted rows atomically, or none if any row fails. Existing saved shows and their immutable snapshots are preserved. Import neither loads playback nor enables scheduling nor grants programme control or local-source consent. Prepare sources again for fresh owner evidence and use the existing separate authorization actions when needed.

Export catalog writes this metadata to a new local .json file you select. Existing files are never overwritten. Owners, author grants, local-source consent, source evidence, saved shows, playback state, credentials and file bytes are excluded. Resource posters require the same client resources; server asset references require matching authorized assets at the destination; local paths require each viewer's own file. Import/export never checks a reference's availability. Keep world and mod backups together: persistence version 3 retains these display hints and reads versions 1 and 2 without changing old programme timing. Restoring an older mod requires its matching pre-upgrade world backup.

The saved authorization permits automatic segment changes and playback controls while the owner is offline; current viewer readiness is still required. mycinema.catalog.programme_authorized: Programme control authorized for this hall. Playback and global scheduling are unchanged.
mycinema.catalog.programme_owner_require: Only the actual owner can perform this programme action. Granting programme or local-source authorization also requires being within 8 blocks of the Control Terminal.
mycinema.catalog.programme_grant_require: Programme authorization is missing. As the owner, use Authorize programme control within 8 blocks of the Control Terminal, then load again.
mycinema.catalog.programme_missing: No saved programme is loaded in this hall. Choose a film and load it first.

mycinema.catalog.programme_ready: Programme ready · waiting for playback confirmation
mycinema.catalog.prepare_epoch_unchanged: Preparation did not establish a new media session. Check the terminal before loading again.
mycinema.catalog.ready_lost: Current viewer readiness was lost. Check the viewer and source before loading again.
mycinema.catalog.restore_required_timeou: The saved media session could not be restored in time. Check the hall and explicitly load the programme again.
mycinema.catalog.prepare_timeout: Programme preparation timed out. Check the source and viewer, then load again.
mycinema.catalog.resume_timeout: The terminal did not confirm the requested playback state in time. Check it before retrying.
mycinema.catalog.source_stopped: The current source stopped before the programme completed. Check the terminal before loading again.
mycinema.catalog.prepare_not_paused: The prepared source was unexpectedly playing. The programme was stopped for review.
mycinema.catalog.awaiting_viewer_timeout: Timed out waiting for a currently ready viewer. Saved owner evidence does not replace viewer readiness.
mycinema.catalog.unverified_duration: The current source has no verified finite duration. Read its metadata before loading again.
mycinema.catalog.duration_mismatch: The current source length differs from this saved programme. Prepare it again and explicitly replace the plan if needed.
mycinema.catalog.revision_unavailable: The current media revision is unavailable. Reload the source before continuing.
mycinema.catalog.external_takeover: Another action replaced this programme’s media session. Control was released without stopping the new session.
mycinema.catalog.stop_unconfirmed: The programme stop was not confirmed. Check this hall before continuing. Reason: %s
mycinema.catalog.diagnostic: Programme action could not complete (reason: %s). Check this hall’s source, viewer and authorization.
mycinema.catalog.unavailable: Programme control is unavailable. Check the hall’s terminal and current media session.
mycinema.catalog.source_not_ready: The current source is not ready. Wait for current viewer metadata and check the hall status.
mycinema.catalog.source_duration_mismatc: The current duration differs from this saved programme. Prepare the source again before replacing its snapshot.
mycinema.catalog.source_live: The current source is live and has no finite programme duration.
mycinema.catalog.source_owner_required: The actual owner must authorize this terminal locally.
mycinema.catalog.source_awaiting_owner_e: Current viewer metadata is available, but this source still needs accepted owner evidence.
mycinema.catalog.prepare_all_hint: Check each unique source in sequence, paused. Clears old library metadata and waits up to 30 seconds per source for fresh owner-client reports. The owner must remain online.
mycinema.catalog.confirm_prepare_all: Validate every source in “%1$s” (revision %2$s; %3$s unique sources) using %4$s? This takes manual control and replaces the hall’s media one source at a time, paused at source 0. Old library metadata is cleared; each source waits up to 30 seconds for a fresh report from the online owner’s client. The server does not decode media. A failure stops the queue; preparing one source or editing the film cancels it. Existing planned snapshots stay unchanged. This does not play the film or enable scheduling.
mycinema.catalog.preparing_all: Validating sources in sequence, paused. Keep the owner online and viewing; up to 30 seconds per source.
mycinema.catalog.local_programme_hint: 1. Authorize programme control for this hall. 2. If needed, separately authorize this film’s local sources. The actual owner must be within 8 blocks to grant consent. It covers only this film revision, TMS and saved sources. Current server saving, game-mode and control permissions still apply. Every viewer needs their own files.
mycinema.catalog.confirm_authorize_local:
Authorize the local sources of “%1$s”, revision %2$s, in %3$s?

Film ID: %7$s
TMS: %4$s
Control Terminal: %5$s

Only the actual owner within 8 blocks of the Control Terminal can grant this, after separately authorizing programme control. Consent is saved for this exact film revision, TMS, ordered normalized sources and their accepted evidence. Changed sources or revisions require new consent.

The server rechecks current administrator or explicit save-and-bypass eligibility and ordinary saving, game-mode and control restrictions every time. Consent cannot override those restrictions. Web-domain rules remain unchanged. This neither starts playback nor enables the global scheduler.

Files are not uploaded or synchronized. Every viewer needs their own readable copy at each local path. This does not prove that different viewers have identical file contents.

Review the full ordered source list below; only local entries receive this consent:
%6$s
mycinema.catalog.confirm_revoke_local_pr:
Revoke all saved local-source consents in %1$s?

TMS: %2$s

Only the actual owner can revoke consent. This clears every film revision’s local-source consent for the selected hall, including consent used by pending and running programmes. Consent-dependent playback is paused immediately and cannot continue using the revoked consent.

A source independently allowed by current server policy remains subject to that policy. Ordinary programme authorization, global scheduler settings and web-domain rules are unchanged. Files and recorded metadata are not removed.
mycinema.catalog.local_programme_authori: Local-source consent saved for this exact film revision and TMS. Playback and global scheduling are unchanged.
mycinema.catalog.local_programme_revoked: Local-source consents revoked for this hall. Consent-dependent playback has been paused; independent server permissions still apply.
mycinema.catalog.local_consent_invalid: Saved local-source consent is invalid. Review the current film and TMS, then authorize the exact film again.
mycinema.catalog.local_consent_limit: Local-source consent storage is full (128 film-revision grants or 1 MiB). Revoke an unused hall’s consents before trying again.
mycinema.catalog.local_source_qualificat: The owner’s current server permissions do not qualify for local-source consent. Current administrator or explicit save-and-bypass eligibility and ordinary media permissions are required.
mycinema.catalog.local_sources_missing: This film revision has no local sources that need local-source consent.
mycinema.catalog.source_local_consent_re: This local source needs consent for the exact saved film revision and TMS. Authorize programme control first, then authorize this film’s local sources.
mycinema.catalog.source_local_source_per: Local-source consent exists, but the owner no longer meets the server’s current media-saving or bypass requirements. Playback is blocked.
mycinema.catalog.programme_delayed: Past the planned end; the saved programme is still preparing, playing or paused. Its full runtime is preserved. Conflicting later shows will be marked missed, without replacing this programme.
mycinema.catalog.programme_completed_lat: Completed naturally after the planned end. The original scheduled times are unchanged.
mycinema.catalog.programme_cancelled: Programme cancelled before confirmed natural completion.
mycinema.catalog.programme_conflict: This hall already has an active programme. It was not replaced.
mycinema.schedule.programme_conflict: Missed: the previous programme still occupied this hall at the scheduled start. It was not interrupted, and this show was not silently moved.
mycinema.catalog.source_scheduled_show_m: The programme’s scheduled record is missing. Playback cannot continue under that claim.

mycinema.manual.chapter.screen_modes.bod:
Right-click your surface to choose Picture, Borrowed media, or Information. Printed signs support Picture and Information with ambient lighting. Content mode is separate from the physical size. Changing mode clears the previous display/controller binding, never starts or stops its movie, and retains editable picture/text settings.

For Information, open Edit information, choose Manual, Hall or Lobby, then use the ordinary management Linking Card for a hall/controller when needed. Independent Manual needs no controller. Guest text still uses display title, public start/end time and known runtime without private media paths.

For Borrowed media, use the Display Linking Card near an owned, loaded TMS, cinema projector, ordinary projector or TV. Then click your loaded LED in Borrowed media mode within 10 minutes. The source and any linked TMS must remain loaded, retain their exact identities and permit mirroring. New placed legacy displays record their mirror claimant. Old unclaimed legacy devices require an explicit nearby administrator claim dialog; this grants picture publication only, not media editing. Shift-use the card on a source to explicitly revoke old mirror references.

The board draws the source texture already opened by that client. It does not open a decoder, duplicate sound, relocate the source’s sound, force chunks, or keep an out-of-range source alive. Different clients still need access to the original source file. Unavailable, replaced, unlinked or revoked sources go blank; reselect and rebind after fixing the cause.
mycinema.manual.chapter.staff_access.bod:
Use the pairing tool on your owned Control Terminal, RFID reader and MyCinema door, while standing on the restricted entry side. Terminal-to-reader range is 128 blocks, reader-to-door range is 16, and pairing requires being within 8 blocks. Double doors pair together.

The RFID reader is a thin wall panel with four horizontal facings. Place it on a sturdy wall face, with its reading face outward; floor and ceiling placement are rejected. Its cyan strip is a fixed locator, not proof of power, accepted access or an open door. Old readers retain their binding; states without facing default north. Existing free-standing readers and readers whose backing is removed remain in place. Check old builds that used the reader as a full-block support.

Use the reader empty-handed or sneak-use a staff card to configure it. Set this door's ENTRY or SERVICE requirement separately from the card role. Select an online employee, keep a blank card in inventory, issue / replace, then give it to that employee. Cards belong to their player and cinema: ENTRY opens every ENTRY reader in that cinema; SERVICE opens ENTRY and SERVICE readers. Cards grant no manager/media control and do not cross controller identities, owners, positions or dimensions.

Adding, re-pairing, replacing or changing a reader, or removing a door, does not revoke employee cards. Replacing hardware still requires pairing it. Changing a reader to SERVICE immediately excludes ENTRY cards there. Moving a reader to another cinema does not move the old grants. Normal entry needs the real loaded reader, controller and complete door.

Issue / replace revokes the selected player's previous cards and their copies for this cinema. Revoke selected player applies across this cinema's readers without affecting other employees or cinemas. You can enter an exact offline UUID to revoke. Valid old cards keep the cinema and original role in their server grant, now usable at all matching readers there; item artwork or NBT cannot upgrade ENTRY to SERVICE.

A swipe opens for about three seconds before closing; external redstone can keep a door open. The paired inside exit still allows manual departure if the controller is unavailable. Managers carry their activated tablet and explicitly right-click the door; there is no proximity opening.

Emergency unlock cinema is available on every manager page to an authorized manager or administrator. Act locally within 8 blocks or hold a currently registered tablet for that loaded controller. The red warning means this cinema's registered doors are held open; it covers the whole cinema, regardless of the selected hall. The override is saved and does not end when you close the menu or restart. Choose Restore normal access and confirm explicitly. Normal leases and redstone resume, so restoration does not guarantee every door shuts immediately.

Loaded registered door leaves reconcile immediately. Unloaded regions are not force-loaded and synchronize when loaded; inspect the awaiting-load count. Old unscoped bindings need their original reader and matching controller loaded, or explicit re-pairing. Removing the controller or detecting a replaced identity/owner retires its old override. Emergency actions do not issue/revoke cards, control media or spend tickets.

Blank, pairing, written, ENTRY and SERVICE artwork only helps recognition. Unpaired map/script doors and paper kumo_staff cards keep their separate datapack behavior; neither normal access nor emergency unlock claims those doors. Keep an independent emergency exit.
mycinema.manual.chapter.seats.title: Seat inventory
mycinema.manual.chapter.seats.body:
Craft a seat binding card from paper and an iron nugget. Use it on your manager to bind and browse. Enroll a hall first. With the bound card, click each existing seat block yourself. Select a hall, enter Lower/Upper or another zone, then row and seat numbers (1–999). Save to register that position.

The manager can hold 4096 entries. Hall + zone + row + number and each block position must be unique in that manager. Owner/operator edits use exact revisions; reload after a conflict. Browse by hall, filter zone and row (0 means all), and inspect status counts. Removing an entry does not break its seat.

Available, Maintenance and Disabled are manually recorded serviceability labels. They do not detect occupants, control furniture, sell tickets or reserve seats. Loaded-only diagnostics report missing/changed blocks or unloaded chunks. They never scan, load chunks, alter counts or replace your chosen status.

Continuous numbering: open Continuous numbering and explicitly set hall, zone, row, start seat, +1 or −1 direction and an optional end (0 means no explicit end). Choose Start / resume; the screen closes. Right-click each existing seat in your chosen order. Only a successful new entry consumes a number. Already registered positions are skipped with a notice; duplicate numbers, denied permission, excessive distance and stale bindings do not advance. The mode stops at the inclusive end or the 1/999 boundary.

Right-click in the air to reopen settings. Next row explicitly increases the row by one and resets the saved original start, direction and end. Row 999 cannot advance. Changed fields need Start / resume; unsaved input is ignored by Next row. Exit numbering or shift-right-click in the air clears the mode while keeping the cinema binding. Shift-right-clicking an ordinary block also opens settings. The card saves its state across reloads, but every click rechecks the same player, controller, dimension and registry revision. If another edit creates a conflict, reload the screen and explicitly resume from the displayed next number. Relinking another cinema clears the mode. It never scans seats, guesses routes or layout, or changes seat blocks.

Physical cinema seats and whole-row numbering: place a Cinema Seat on a solid full-height top surface, facing the screen. Top slabs support the chair; lower slabs and fences do not. Its selection and collision use the actual chair shape. Right-click to sit; the occupied mount exists only while someone is seated. Leave a clear footwell and headroom for a safe exit. Breaking and replacing a chair creates a different physical identity. Verify seating pose and collision in the actual client after changing models or resources.

For a complete row, bind the existing seat card at the manager and open Whole-row numbering. Choose auditorium, zone, row display (numeric or plain letters A, B, ... Z, AA), starting number and ascending/descending order. Begin selection, then right-click the first and last real cinema chairs in one level straight row, up to 128 blocks. The list previews every chair and gap. Gaps and already registered chairs do not consume a new number. Wrong blocks, changed identities, mixed facing, protected cells or number conflicts block the entire batch. Confirm only after reviewing it; no partial row is written.

A preview expires after five minutes and is rechecked on confirmation. Next row advances the row label and starts a new endpoint selection. Shift-right-click air exits either numbering mode. Small windows can scroll the form or use Page Up/Page Down; the top Close button remains available. Existing block-only records remain unverified and are never silently reassigned to a replacement chair. Remove an old binding explicitly before registering a new identity. Physical chairs claimed by another cinema cannot be batch-bound.

Installing MyCinema does not demolish, rebuild or migrate an existing map automatically.

Double Support Cinema Seat is an additional style using the original auditorium artwork and nine textures, uniformly scaled to fit one cell. The default Cinema Seat is retained. Both styles use physical seat identity, controller ownership, and whole-row numbering. A mixed row records the actual style of each chair. Removing and replacing a chair creates a new identity; changing style is not an automatic migration. Verify each style's seating pose and collision in the actual client; measurements for one style do not apply to another.
mycinema.manual.chapter.row_guides.title: Row guides and C&B tags
mycinema.manual.chapter.row_guides.body:
Craft four MyCinema guide tags with three paper in the top row and an iron nugget below the center. Place a tag on a block side for a wall guide, or on a sturdy upper face for a horizontal floor decal. A floor decal is half a pixel thick, has no walking collision and faces you in one of four horizontal directions. Full blocks, upper slabs and double slabs are supported. Lower slabs and incomplete upper faces are rejected rather than leaving a floating gap. Removing or lowering its support drops one ordinary tag. Copy saved before breaking a configured tag if you want to reuse its text; each new placement chooses its own attachment and facing. Enter hall/zone captions and first/last row indices (1–999). Choose numeric 1, 2, 3 or letters A, B, C. Numeric rows can be plain, ROW-prefixed, or legacy R. Letter rows always have no prefix: A, Z, AA, A-H. The prefix control is disabled for letters, and older letter presets with R/ROW normalize to plain on load. Numeric indices remain unchanged: 1=A, 26=Z, 27=AA, 702=ZZ, 703=AAA, 999=ALK. Preview shows the full label. This changes display only, never seat identity or inventory numbering.

For an aisle entrance, enter both first and last seat numbers as well as the row range. An illustrative synthetic guide is A-H · S1-12 with a manually selected left arrow; S identifies seat numbers. Enter the actual ranges yourself: the mod does not know your left entrance or which seats it serves. Both seat-range fields at 0 mean no seat range. Alternatively, Single seat above 0 creates an old-style single-row seat label; it cannot be combined with a seat range. Row and seat indices are 1–999, and each range must be ascending.

You choose every arrow, zone, entrance, route and sign position. Save, then hold guide tags in either hand and choose Copy saved to reuse the saved scheme, numeric prefix, both ranges and arrow. Draft changes must be saved first. No route is inferred. Older row-only and single-seat presets remain compatible.

Optional Chisels & Bits: install NeoForge 21.1.32. In creative mode, leave an empty inventory slot, save and choose C&B (creative). The 16×16×1-bit face keeps old row-only/single-seat layouts intact. For combined ranges, one line shows the complete row range and the other the complete S-prefixed seat range. A thin 1 and dash allow common A-H / S1-12 and A-H / S1-24 examples to fit. Each proportional line must fit 16 pixels: larger combinations are explicitly refused, never cropped or silently shortened. The normal MyCinema text guide still displays both full ranges. Numeric ROW tags use a compact header and separate arrow; letters have no prefix. Captions remain in the item name.

C&B's readable front faces north. Place/rotate it yourself; the back of a one-bit sheet is mirrored. Generation requires 16 bits per side and creative mode until survival costs are defined. Missing/unsupported C&B reports an error without world changes. MyCinema tags work independently.

Control Terminal: %4$s
TMS: %2$s
Projectors:
%3$s

All three devices must still have no recorded owner and retain these exact identities and reciprocal bindings. Devices that already have an owner cannot be taken over.

This stops current playback at zero and puts this hall in manual mode. Media addresses, playlist, original save author, projection geometry, volume and calibration are preserved. Pending plans remain; any running show becomes manually overridden.
